ka: Ka letter (consonant) that is the first letter in 33 consonants. Kaṇṭhaja Lahu Ka letter (consonant). Tipi,5,1 ka ka(pu) (1) Brahma. (2) The body. (3) Air. (4) The sun. (50 Fire. (6) Peacock. (7) A man. (8) The land (or) ground. Tipi,5,1 ka ka(na) [kara+kvi. Dhāna, ṭī. 661.] (1) Wealth (or) peaceful and tranquil. (2) Water. See also - Kānana, Kamala. (4) Lotus. See - Kesara. Ka(ti) (1) One who is famous. (2) A small (object or thing). Tipi,5,2 Ka. This Ka letter is in the middle of a word, (meaningless) that is just to connect words. Tipi,5,2 ka(ti). This ka is at the end of a word. There has Ṇa Anubana in the Vuddhi word. (1) Reproach. (2) Pity. (2) A small (or) young object. (3) Disgusted thing. (5) The meaning of its dependent word (Ka that is not its own meaning) (6) Combination. Show obviously. (8) Produce sound. (9) One"s own wealth. (10) Born. Being (or) happening (or) Arising. (11) Living. (12) Connected. Having. (13) The extent. (14) The matter. Behavior. (15) A cause of arising. (16) Should be done. (17) The name (or) designation. (A bird called Moraka due to be similar to a peacock). (3) Similar (or) Uniform. (19) Chanting. (20) Teaching. (21) Understand.  (22) Skillful. (23) Completion. Having. (24) The body. (25) It is not obvious. (26) A little. (27) Short. (28) Recites the meaning two times. (29) It carries out. It causes. (30) Can hold on. (31) Having (or) eating. Ka(ti) what is it? Who are you? = Meaning of asking. (This Ka comes from kiṃ Sadda. See detail in Kiṃ).

kacca:
[Kara+tvā]  CL=9 1. 'ပြုပြီး၍' - 'Having done' or 'After completing'
2. 'kacca  (m)' , 'kacca' is derived from the root 'kaca' (meaning 'to shine') plus a suffix. The forms 'kacceti', 'kaccayati', and 'kacco'.
4. These terms are also called (vuccanti) kaccānāti, kaccāyanāti, or kātiyānāti.
5.The primordial person called Kacca, the sage who existed in ancient times.

kacchū: [Kaca+ukaca-bandhane] (thī) CL=7 [U, cassa chattaṃ, dvittādi. Dhānaṭī, 327.]  Itch. Scab. (Some translate it as ringworm).
kaccāna: [Kacca+ṇāna] (ti) CL=7 [In Thī kaccānī. Sakaṭassa apaccaṃ sākaṭāyano sākaṭāno---kaccāyanaṃ kaccānaṃ---kaccāyanī kaccānī. Kaccaññaḥ. 345. Kaccassa putto kaccāyano kaccāno. Rū. 366 - See also]. One who is a lineage of Kacca. (A) One who is being in the Kaccāna race. (B) A Thera is named Kaccāna. Arhaṅamahākaccaya Thera. See an elaborate version in Kaccānatthera. (C) A homeless spiritual seeker is named Kaccāna. A homeless spiritual seeker is named Vekhanasa. Lord  A homeless spiritual seeker is named Vekhanasa and is called Kaccāna by Lord Buddha. (D) A Thera is named Kaccāna. A Thera is named Kaccāna Gotta. (E) A young man named Kaccaya. It is the past existence (life)"s name of an Ogre Puṇṇaka. (Thi) (F) A woman named Kaccānī who is in Kaccāna lineage.
kaccānagotta: [Kaccāna+gotta] (na) CL=7 Kaccāna lineage. This lineage is one of the president"s lineage. Kaccānagotta(ti) [kaccānagotta+ṇa] (1) One who is being in Kaccāna lineage. (Pu) (2) A Thera who named Kaccānagotta. When Lord Buddha dwells in Sāvatthi Country, he asked Lord Buddha about Sammādiṭṭhi, so Lord Buddha preaches about Dvayanissitokhvāhaṃ kaccāna, etc., When Venerable Ānandā preaches Venerable Channa that is making reference the upper dhamma as per Lord Buddha"s teaching. See also - Kaccāna-(C). (Thi) (3) A woman who is in Kaccāna lineage.
kaccānapeyyāla:
[Kaccāna+peyyāla]  CL=9 The Mahakassana Bhaddekaratta Sutta, also known as the Kassana Payaya Sutta.
(kaccānapeyyālasutakho mahākaccāna bhaddekarattasuta)

kakkhaḷa:
[Kara+ḷa]  CL=10 1. 'Kibbisaṃ karotīti kakkhaḷo' - One who does evil is called kakkhaḷo.
Reference: Mogg. 7.227
Word formation: kakkha + ala, where "la" becomes "ḷa"
Reference: Dhātu. Ṭī. 71
2. Meanings:
(1) Hard
(a) Hard (physical matter)
(b) Solid (like stone or other objects)
(c) Hard (sound)
(2) Cruel, fierce, savage
(3) Rough
(a) Rough, harsh (speech)
(b) Rough, bad (dream)
(c) Rough, unruly (defilements, etc.)
(d) Rough, bad, violent (rebellion)
(e) Verbally abusive, one who speaks in an opposing or confrontational manner
(f) One with a rough heart, stubborn, mentally rough person
(g) Intense, severe
See 'ghoravisa' .
